source.title: The Velvet Spark
source.overview: You read every shift in the room before deciding where to stand.
source.howYouMove: Quick, polished, and mentally agile. Conversation stays smooth, momentum stays sharp, and reactions tend to arrive faster than people expect. The presence feels easy, but there is constant calculation underneath it.
shadows: Talks around tension instead of naming it
Keeps too many angles open at once
source.emotionalPattern: A lot gets processed in real time, but not everything is felt all the way through before the next response arrives. What looks effortless is often a fast internal adjustment
source.loveStyle: Closeness needs chemistry, intelligence, and a sense of movement. Interest stays high when the dynamic feels alive, but emotional steadiness can get replaced by soft management when vulnerability feels too slow
source.friendshipStyle: Easy to like, easy to talk to, and usually the first to catch what is changing in a group. Loyalty is real, but attention can scatter when too many dynamics need to be tracked at once
source.workStyle: Works through wit, speed, and responsiveness. The strength is social intelligence with speed, but it weakens when too much energy goes into positioning instead of deciding
source.growthPath: State the real position sooner. Close the side doors
source.compatibilityNotes: Works best with people who are sharp but steady, and who do not confuse lightness with lack of depth

source.title: The Silk Pillar
source.overview: You preserve harmony long after your position has hardened.
source.howYouMove: Calm, even, and dependable. Responses tend to be thoughtful rather than rushed, and the overall presence feels grounded even in complicated rooms. There is softness here, but not fragility.
strengths: Brings calm into emotionally noisy situations
Holds a clear line without theatrics
shadows: Stays fixed long after adjustment is needed
Avoids direct conflict but hardens underneath
source.emotionalPattern: Feelings move slowly but deeply. What seems calm on the outside is often a long process of weighing, containing, and deciding what deserves a response
source.loveStyle: Closeness works best when it feels loyal, respectful, and emotionally stable. Trust builds slowly here, but once it lands it runs deep. The difficulty comes when silence is used to hold a line that should be spoken aloud
source.friendshipStyle: Steady and dependable in ways people remember. This identity does not spread itself everywhere, but the bonds it keeps are durable and hard to shake
source.workStyle: Works with patience, discipline, and social tact. The strength is durable presence, but it weakens when flexibility is treated like compromise instead of intelligence
source.growthPath: Stop smoothing what needs to be said. Release the line before it becomes a wall
source.compatibilityNotes: Works best with people who are grounded, respectful, and emotionally clear enough to meet steadiness without trying to force speed
